summary: The ANSO-CAS-TWAS/UNESCO PhD Scholarship funds a PhD at the University of Science and Technology of China (USTC) or the University of Chinese Academy of Sciences (UCAS) for nationals of developing countries. It waives tuition and pays 6,000 or 7,000 CNY a month for up to four years, with health insurance, one flight to China and a visa allowance. The last call closed on 31 January 2026, and the next has not been announced.
meta_title: ANSO-CAS-TWAS PhD Scholarship in China: stipend and eligibility
meta_description: A funded PhD at USTC or UCAS for nationals of developing countries: tuition waived, 6,000 to 7,000 CNY a month for four years and a flight to China.
covers: A tuition waiver and an application fee waiver.
A monthly stipend of 6,000 or 7,000 CNY, depending on a qualification test, for up to 48 months.
One international flight from your home country to China and a one-time visa allowance, paid by TWAS/UNESCO if you are eligible.
eligibility: Nationals of eligible developing countries in the South who do not hold Chinese citizenship.
Born on or after 1 January 1991, for the PhD.
Least developed countries and women receive special, non-exclusive consideration.
how_to_apply: Apply for a PhD through the USTC or UCAS admission system and choose the CAS-ANSO Scholarship.
Tick the ANSO-CAS-TWAS/UNESCO box in the application.
Watch TWAS's PhD fellowships page for the next call; the last one closed on 31 January 2026.
watch_out: You can apply for only one programme a calendar year across TWAS and OWSD fellowships.
The flight and visa items are paid by TWAS/UNESCO only if you are eligible.
The next call's dates are not yet announced.
costs: A stipend of 6,000 or 7,000 CNY a month
documents: The USTC or UCAS online PhD application, with the CAS-ANSO Scholarship selected
The ANSO-CAS-TWAS/UNESCO option ticked in the same application
Evidence that you are a national of an eligible developing country

faq.q: Can Africans apply for the ANSO-CAS-TWAS PhD Scholarship?
faq.a: It is for nationals of eligible developing countries in the South, with special consideration for least developed countries. Check your country on TWAS's list of developing countries.
Tuition is waived and the stipend is 6,000 or 7,000 CNY a month for up to four years, with health insurance and a flight to China.
Not announced yet. The last call closed on 31 January 2026.
